glossary.definition: Standard precautions apply to every patient. Add gloves, gown, mask, and eye protection according to likely contact with blood, body fluids, mucous membranes, nonintact skin, or contaminated equipment.
Perform hand hygiene at indicated moments and after glove removal. Gloves do not replace hand hygiene.
Immediately wash or flush the exposed area, report the event, and follow the organization's exposure evaluation process.

slides.speaker_script: Standard Precautions and Exposure Prevention. Select hand hygiene and protective equipment from the anticipated exposure, then remove equipment without contaminating clean areas. Five lanes carry the lesson: anticipate exposure, hand hygiene, exposure response, apply, evaluate.

slides.speaker_script: Start with one cue. A procedure may splash body fluid toward the face. Decide what you would do before the lesson tells you, and hold on to it; the same cue returns as the first assessment item.

slides.speaker_script: One minute, before any of this is taught. These three headings are the whole lesson in order, but they are shuffled on the slide. Getting the order wrong here is more useful than getting it right: it shows you which move you would have skipped under pressure.

slides.learning_objective: Choose the correct action for a single cue.
answer_key: C. Perform hand hygiene immediately after glove removal.
slides.speaker_script: One question, and it targets the middle of the lesson. The cue is: Gloves are removed after contact with contaminated material. Read all four options and commit to one before the reveal, because the value of a checkpoint is in being wrong out loud rather than quietly. The reasoning you are being tested on is this: Gloves can have defects and hands can be contaminated during removal.

card_data.stem: Gloves are removed after contact with contaminated material. What should the nurse do?
options: A. Delay action until the end of the shift.
B. Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
C. Perform hand hygiene immediately after glove removal.
D. Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.
card_data.rationale: Gloves can have defects and hands can be contaminated during removal.

slides.learning_objective: Respond to a cue using the lesson's frame.
slides.activity_prompt: Two sentences: what you assess, then what you do.
answer_key: Wash the area, report promptly, and begin the exposure protocol.
Immediate cleansing and timely evaluation reduce preventable harm and enable indicated prophylaxis.
slides.speaker_script: A bedside moment, and this time you write rather than choose. The situation: A nurse sustains a needlestick injury. Write two sentences before the debrief: one naming what you assess, one naming what you do about it. Keep them in that order, because the order is the judgement. The keyed reasoning is: Immediate cleansing and timely evaluation reduce preventable harm and enable indicated prophylaxis.

slides.learning_objective: Sort cues by whether they require immediate action.
slides.activity_prompt: Place each cue and justify one.
answer_key: Act now: the cues whose keyed action is immediate
Act in sequence: the cues whose keyed action is verification or planning
slides.speaker_script: Two columns, and the sorting rule is the point of the slide. Put a cue on the left when delay changes the outcome for the patient, and on the right when the correct action is verification, planning or teaching that a short delay does not worsen. Justify one of your placements aloud. Learners who can sort these reliably are the ones who prioritise well under load.

slides.learning_objective: Record the lesson's decisions in a reusable frame.
slides.speaker_script: These are the fields the topic asks you to be able to fill in for any patient. If you cannot complete one, that is the part of the assessment still to do.

slides.slide_title: Capstone: choose the next safe action
slides.learning_objective: Select the priority action in the lesson's hardest cue.
answer_key: B. Activate the safety device and place the needle directly in an approved sharps container.
slides.speaker_script: The last question, and the hardest cue the topic carries: A nurse plans to recap a used needle by hand. All four options are things a nurse might plausibly do, which is what makes it a capstone rather than a checkpoint. Choose the priority action, not merely a defensible one. The reasoning that separates them: Avoiding manipulation of used sharps reduces percutaneous injury risk.

card_data.scenario: A nurse plans to recap a used needle by hand.
card_data.stem: What is the priority nursing action?
options: A. Delay action until the end of the shift.
B. Activate the safety device and place the needle directly in an approved sharps container.
C. Document the finding without reassessment or follow-up.
D. Delegate the clinical judgment decision to unlicensed assistive personnel.
card_data.rationale: Avoiding manipulation of used sharps reduces percutaneous injury risk.

slides.speaker_script: Close the loop with no notes. Answer each of these aloud or on paper, one per lane of the lesson.
